An optional half-texel inset pulls each rect in from the cell edge so nearest/linear sampling never bleeds a neighbouring cell at the seam.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.AnimationClip**: A named skeletal animation — a set of per-joint s plus the clip's total . Sampled at a time in [0, Duration] (the app loops/clamps as it likes) to produce per-joint local transforms, which the animation runtime composes down the skeleton into the bone palette. Backend-neutral, immutable; the natural output of a glTF animation. One clip drives one skeleton.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.AnimationInterpolation**: How an animation track interpolates between keyframes — mirrors glTF's sampler interpolation modes.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.JointChannel**: One joint's animated transform within an — any of its translation, rotation, and scale may be keyed. A null track means that component is not animated by this clip and the joint's bind-pose value () is used instead. Backend-neutral, immutable.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.QuaternionTrack**: A keyframed animation channel — a joint's rotation over time. The are strictly increasing seconds; [i] is the (unit) rotation at Times[i]. Linear interpolation slerps between the surrounding keyframes. Backend-neutral, immutable.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.Skeleton**: A mesh's skeleton: a flat joint array (in glTF skin order) where each joint records its parent index (-1 for a root), its inverse bind matrix, and its bind-pose local transform. The parents form a forest and may appear in any order — the animation runtime resolves world matrices accordingly, so no topological sort is assumed. Backend-neutral (System.Numerics), immutable — the natural output of a glTF skin. The animation runtime composes a clip's sampled local transforms down this hierarchy into joint world matrices, then multiplies each by its entry to get the bone palette the skinning shader applies. A 's joint indices reference this array (and thus the palette slots). is the fallback when a clip leaves a joint (or a joint's translation/rotation/scale) un-keyed.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.SkinnedVertex**: A skinned mesh's bind-pose vertex: the canonical fields plus the two skinning attributes — four bone indices and four blend weights. 80 bytes, sequentially packed, mirroring (POSITION 0, NORMAL 12, TEXCOORD 24, TANGENT 32, JOINTS 48, WEIGHTS 64). Backend-neutral (System.Numerics + plain uints, no graphics-API types). The joint indices reference the mesh's joint array (and thus the bone-palette slot the compute skinning pass multiplies by); the weights sum to 1 (the glTF importer renormalizes). A vertex bound to fewer than four joints sets the unused weights to 0 (their joint index is then irrelevant).
- **Loom.Core.Animation.Vector3Track**: A keyframed animation channel — a joint's translation or scale over time. The are strictly increasing seconds; [i] is the value at Times[i]. The two arrays have equal length (≥ 1). Backend-neutral, immutable.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Bounds**: An axis-aligned bounding box (Min/Max corners). The unit of coarse visibility: a mesh carries a local-space box, an instance transforms it to world space, and the CPU frustum cull tests it against the camera's . Backend-neutral pure math (System.Numerics), like — culling is an app-owned optimization the engine offers, never a scene graph it mandates ("you hand me draw lists").
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Frustum**: A view frustum as six inward-facing s (left, right, bottom, top, near, far) in world space — the debug camera's "what would be visible" volume and the engine's optional CPU frustum-cull primitive. Each plane is oriented so the inside half-space is positive ( ≥ 0). Built from a view-projection matrix via ; composed entirely of types (no bespoke math). Extracted from the neutral view-projection (right-handed, +Y up, z ∈ [0,1] — the host's CreatePerspectiveFieldOfView convention), so culling is backend-independent: the per-backend clip-space Y-flip only affects rasterization NDC, not which world objects are in view.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Matrix4x4FrustumExtensions**: C# 14 extension members on for frustum math — kept on the BCL type per the project convention (use ; add missing operations as extension members, not a bespoke helper class). The receiver is a row-vector view-projection (clip = world · viewProjection).
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Mesh**: An opaque handle to GPU-resident geometry (vertex + index buffers), minted by the engine when the app uploads a mesh and handed back to passes via . Like , it is just an identity the backend resolves to real buffers — the describe layer never sees the GPU resources. Meshes are app-owned, stable resources (the app builds them once and keeps them), so referencing one from a pass's record closure does not break the closure's purity the way capturing per-frame data would ("you hand me draw lists").
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.OverlayVertex**: The vertex of a 2D overlay draw list — the universal shape for screen-space, painter-ordered geometry (UI, immediate-mode overlays, a textured quad): a pixel-space position, a texture coordinate, a premultiplied colour, and a float4 of per-vertex data the consuming technique defines. Backend-neutral (System.Numerics + ), [StructLayout] sequential so it uploads as verbatim.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Vertex**: Loom's canonical interleaved vertex: position, normal, UV, and a tangent. One fixed layout for now — enough to drive the reference frame's geometry plus normal mapping. Backend-neutral (System.Numerics, no graphics-API types), so the backend owns the vertex-layout description that mirrors these fields. Shaders that don't read the tangent simply ignore the extra attribute.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexAttribute**: One attribute in a : a semantic name plus its element format. The semantic is the neutral link between the data and the shader — Vulkan binds by [[vk::location]] (assigned in order), DirectX12 binds by HLSL semantic name + index (the index derived from how many earlier attributes share the name, so four "ITRANSFORM" rows become ITRANSFORM0..3). Semantic names map 1:1 onto glTF attribute names (POSITION, NORMAL, TEXCOORD, TANGENT, …), which is what makes an importer's output drop straight into a layout (glTF).
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexFormat**: Backend-neutral vertex-attribute formats — the element type of one attribute in a . Deliberately separate from (which is render-target / texture oriented and has no three-component float concept): a vertex attribute is just a small tuple of 32-bit floats today. The backend maps each to its concrete API format (e.g. → VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32_SFLOAT / DXGI_FORMAT_R32G32B32_FLOAT). Grow this deliberately as layouts need more (packed colours, integer bone indices for skinning).
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexFormatExtensions**: Helpers over — kept here so the enum stays a plain value list.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexInputRate**: How the input assembler advances through a 's buffer.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexLayout**: A backend-neutral description of one vertex stream: an ordered attribute set, the byte offset of each attribute (tight-packed in declaration order), the resulting stride, and whether the input assembler advances or (and which binding slot it occupies). A is uploaded against a layout, a technique declares the layout(s) it consumes, and the backend builds its pipeline vertex-input + bind stride from them. The layout is the shared contract between a mesh and the technique that draws it — a stride mismatch is a clear engine error, not a silent corruption. Backend-neutral by construction (no graphics-API type), so the same layout drives Vulkan and DirectX12. It is the natural output of an asset importer too — a glTF loader reads accessors and emits a layout + packed buffer — assets are loader-owned, Core never gains a decode dependency.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.AccessKind**: How a single pass touches a single resource. These edges are the entire input to the Execute layer: ordering, barriers, layout transitions and aliasing are all derived from them The vs distinction is load-bearing — it tells the barrier-deriver whether the contents are produced (clearable) or accumulated onto.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.BlendMode**: How a technique's colour output combines with what is already in the target — technique state, not pass state ("additive-ness is technique state, not pass state"). It pairs with a pass that .Blends its target: the graph derives that the existing contents must be preserved and read-modify-written; this enum picks the blend equation the backend bakes into the pipeline. Backend-neutral — the backend maps each value to its own blend-state representation (Vulkan blend factors, D3D12 blend desc).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.BufferHandle**: A GPU storage buffer (not an image). A compute pass .ReadWrites it and a draw .ReadsVertex it (GPU particles). Sized in bytes, not resolution-bound.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ColorHandle**: A colour image target. Produced by .Writes/.Blends, read by .Samples, and (as a storage image — e.g. the persistent exposure value) by .ReadWrites. Also the static type of the and image handles, which are colour-like (their distinct lifetime is carried by ).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ConstantsHandle**: An app-writable parameter buffer (a uniform/constant buffer). Created with , filled per frame (or on change) by handle via IEngine.Write, and bound to a technique's reflected uniform slot by a pass that .Reads it. Sized to sizeof(T); the struct written through Write must match the shader's uniform-block layout on both backends (std140 / cbuffer packing — prefer float4 rows).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.CullMode**: Which triangle faces a technique discards before rasterizing — fixed-function rasterizer state the backend bakes into the pipeline, not pass state. Like it is intent that reflection can't infer, so the technique states it; the backend maps each value to its own representation (Vulkan VkCullModeFlags, D3D12 D3D12_CULL_MODE). Loom's front-face winding is counter-clockwise in screen space (the glTF convention and Vulkan's default), and both backends are configured to agree on it — so discards the same triangles whichever backend renders, preserving cross-backend parity.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.DepthHandle**: A depth/stencil target. Written by .WritesDepth, tested by .ReadsDepth, and sampleable.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.Domain**: A resolution domain: everything declared in it renders at ×. This is the mechanism behind pixelation — render the whole world into a small domain, then cross to the backbuffer with an explicit nearest-neighbour upscale. A Domain is an immutable façade over the owning : its / verbs declare targets into that builder. Obtain one from or .
- **Loom.Core.Graph.Format**: Backend-neutral render-graph attachment / target pixel formats — an abstract vocabulary the backend maps to a concrete API format (e.g. Rgba8Srgb → VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB). Keep this list free of any graphics-API type so Loom.Core stays portable. Grow it deliberately as effects need more. Deliberately distinct from (the source-image / sampled-encoding vocabulary): the two overlap on the plain RGBA8 encodings on purpose, but diverge as render targets gain HDR/packed/depth formats while source textures gain block-compressed ones. Keep them separate rather than unifying.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.GraphBuilder**: The fluent entry point for authoring a render graph (the g in DefineGraph(g => { … })). Declare resolution domains and resources, then passes that state their reads/writes. Build is ordinary C#: feature toggles are control flow, not config. Call to drive one and get the immutable back. Backbuffer spelling. The swapchain colour target is exposed directly as the handle: var screen = g.Backbuffer; … .Writes(screen); reach the native-resolution domain for sibling targets via g.Backbuffer.Domain.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.GraphPass**: An immutable, baked pass: its name, kind, queue, the resource-access edges it declared, and its per-frame record callback. Produced by when the graph is built; never mutated thereafter. The callback is excluded from the graph hash (it's frame data, not structure).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.IStorageBufferHandle**: A handle that can be .Reads'd as a shader storage buffer (a read-only SSBO / StructuredBuffer<T>) — an app-writable structured array (). The marker lets reject category errors at compile time, exactly as does for a uniform block. Distinct from , which marks a read-write compute target (.ReadWrites).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.IStorageHandle**: A handle that can be .ReadWrites'd (general read-modify-write storage): a storage image or a buffer.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ITextureHandle**: A handle that can be .Samples'd (read in a shader): a colour or depth image.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.IUniformHandle**: A handle that can be .Reads'd as a shader uniform/constant input — an app-writable parameter buffer (). The marker lets reject category errors at compile time, exactly as / do for their verbs.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.PassBuilder**: The fluent builder for a single pass. You state only what the pass reads and writes — every verb records a edge and returns this for chaining. Ordering, barriers and layout transitions are derived from these edges by the Execute layer; any verb that asked you to state order would be a design smell.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.PassKind**: Whether a pass records graphics draws or a compute dispatch.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.Queue**: The logical queue a pass is assigned to. Backend-neutral, and reserved for a future multi-queue scheduler: the enum and the .Queue(...) verb exist so the authoring surface is forward-compatible, but the Execute layer builds a single linear timeline and both backends are single-queue, so is not yet honoured. Declaring it makes graph derivation fail loudly, rather than silently running the pass on the graphics queue and giving a false impression of overlap.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.RenderGraph**: An immutable, baked render-graph description: domains, resources, passes (with their access edges) and the present target. This is the whole output of the Describe layer — it carries intent only; no ordering, barriers, or GPU types (those are derived by the Execute layer). It is hashable () so the bake cache can recognise an unchanged graph, and dumpable () for inspection and tests. Authored via .
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ResourceAccess**: One edge in the graph: a pass touches a resource in a particular way. The complete set of these across all passes is the only thing the Execute layer needs to derive ordering and barriers.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ResourceHandle**: An immutable handle to a declared resource — the currency the authoring API trades in. You get one from a verb (or / / ) and hand it to pass verbs (.Writes, .Samples, …). This is an abstract base; every concrete handle is a , , or . The subtypes let the pass verbs reject category errors at compile time (you cannot .WritesDepth a colour target, .Samples a buffer, etc.) rather than at bake time The marker interfaces (sampleable) and (read-write storage) capture the capabilities verbs constrain against. Identity is by reference: a handle is the resource, so ping-pong is just swapping two handles in a normal loop. Structural hashing lives on , which walks handles by their stable — never on the handle itself, whose back-reference must not leak into a hash.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ResourceKind**: What a declared resource fundamentally is. This is a property of the declaration, not of how passes use it — storage-image / sampled / attachment usage is derived from the access edges ("derived, not declared"), never stated here.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.StorageBufferHandle**: An app-writable storage buffer (a read-only SSBO / StructuredBuffer<T>). Created with , filled per frame (or on change) by handle via IEngine.Write with a span, and bound to a technique's reflected storage-buffer slot by a pass that .Reads it. The bigger sibling of : an array, for data too large or too dynamically-indexed for a uniform block. Sized to count × sizeof(T); the element type written through Write must match the shader's structured-buffer element layout. When the count is an initial capacity and a larger Write grows the allocation.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.DrawCall**: A single raster draw command for . Collapses the per-axis overloads into one descriptor: geometry source (mesh / skinned / procedural), instancing (none / CPU / GPU), material, and extra inputs (uniforms or sampled). All fields default to their zero/null values.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.DrawCall.InstanceSource**: The per-instance data for a : CPU-sourced (uploaded per frame) or GPU-resident. Construct via or ; the default is empty (single draw).
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.DrawCommand**: One run of an submission: a contiguous slice of the index stream, drawn under its own scissor rectangle with one texture bound. This is the backend-neutral draw-list command — the same shape Dear ImGui and the game-UI compositor batch into (a clip rect + a texture + an index range), generalized so any per-frame variable-size indexed stream can be submitted through the public API.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.DrawListData**: One frame's flattened draw list — a variable-size vertex stream, its 16-bit index stream, and the batched s that scissor + texture + index-range it. Backend-neutral (no graphics-API types), so the whole producer pipeline up to GPU upload is CPU-testable against — the draw-list analog of the render graph's BarrierPlan/AliasPlan snapshots. A producer (the UI compositor) hands a set of these in via ; a pass submits one through . Rebuilt only when its source changes; an unchanged frame re-submits the same .
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.DrawListId**: Identifies one draw list a frame may carry in . A producer (e.g. the UI host's compositor) assigns a stable id per list — the screen-space overlay and each in-world surface get a distinct one — and a pass names it to submit that list (). Backend-neutral managed data, like .
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.Engine**: The backend registry and the host's entry point to rendering. Each referenced backend assembly self-registers an here (via a module initializer) as it loads, so the host discovers what is available at runtime and selects one by name: var backend = Engine.AvailableEngines.FirstOrDefault(e => e.Name == settings.PreferredBackend) ?? Engine.AvailableEngines.First(); using var engine = backend.Create(window.VkSurface, width, height, settings); Which backends are present is decided by the build (the <UseVulkan>/ <UseDirectX12> flags pull in the assemblies); which present backend runs is the runtime selection above. A backend's module initializer fires when its assembly is first touched — constructing the backend's subclass (the one sanctioned place a backend type appears in app code) is enough to load it before is read.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.EngineSettings**: Backend-neutral engine configuration — the canonical config object a host populates and hands to , replacing the scattered constructor args and environment variables of earlier milestones. A host may read environment variables into it, but the object is the source of truth. Subclass it per backend (VulkanEngineSettings, a future DirectX12EngineSettings) to carry backend-only knobs (preferred adapter, required extensions); the neutral engine surface only ever reads the base properties, and a backend down-casts to read its own.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.FrameInputs**: The per-frame data a host hands the engine for one call. This is the single channel for everything that varies frame to frame — timing and the UI draw data — so pass closures stay pure: they pull these from rather than capturing host state. Immutable: the host builds a fresh one each frame. View-projections are not here: the app publishes them as ordinary data through the g.Constants buffers its passes read, so the engine carries no camera or view concept.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.IEngine**: A live rendering engine — the backend-neutral front door the host codes against. It owns the long-lived device and the pipeline cache; the active graph is swappable (), so a structural change re-derives the schedule/barriers/aliasing while the device and cache are reused. Obtain one from via ; the host names no graphics-API type to drive it. Dispose it to tear the device down (drains the GPU first).
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.IEngineClipSpace**: Exposes the engine's clip-space convention as a neutral matrix, so an app-side view (a Loom.Concepts.Camera) can compose it into a view-projection without naming a backend's NDC convention. Shaders are single-source bytecode, so the Vulkan/D3D12 NDC difference lives in this matrix rather than in the shader: an app computes view * projection * ClipSpaceCorrection and the result lands in the engine's clip space on every backend. A narrow capability interface (rather than passing the whole ) so a camera depends only on this — and can take null for it, meaning "no correction" (a test, or a +Y-up-native target that needs none).
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.InspectableResource**: A graph image resource the debug viewer can preview. Backend-neutral — no GPU type; the host enumerates these from and binds one into a draw list via .
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.IRenderBackend**: A rendering backend — the factory for an on a particular graphics API (Vulkan today, a future DirectX12). Backends self-register into ; the host picks one by at runtime and calls . This is the seam that lets a second backend slot in without touching the describe/execute layers.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.IRenderContext**: The per-frame execution context handed to a pass's .Draw/.Dispatch callback. Callbacks pull their inputs from here rather than capturing them, which is what keeps the graph description frame-independent and cacheable. Techniques are addressed by name — the string a pass passes to a draw verb matching a registration.
- **Loom.Core.Hosting.PassTiming**: One leaf pass's GPU wall time for a completed frame. Backend-neutral — no graphics-API types; the backend fills these from timestamp queries read back after the frame's fence.
- **Loom.Core.Materials.Material**: An opaque handle to an ordered bundle of s, minted by the engine via and handed to a draw through . The material supplies the textures that fill a technique's reflected sampler slots, in declaration order (texture 0 → the shader's binding 0, and so on); the technique still selects the pipeline, so the same material can be drawn into a G-buffer pass and skipped by a depth-only/shadow pass (which reflects no samplers) without change. Like and it is just an identity the backend resolves — the describe layer never sees the GPU resources, and the ordered texture list lives backend-side so the draw path binds with zero allocation. A material is textures only. A per-material scalar/parameter block (tints, roughness factors) can be added without changing this handle.
- **Loom.Core.Materials.MipLevel**: One level of a texture's mip chain: tightly packed RGBA8 (row pitch = Width*4, no padding). The backend re-pads to its own row-pitch rules on upload.
- **Loom.Core.Materials.SamplerAddress**: How a technique's sampler treats texture coordinates outside [0,1] — technique state the backend bakes into its sampler (Vulkan VkSamplerAddressMode, D3D12 D3D12_TEXTURE_ADDRESS_MODE). Like and , it is fixed-function intent reflection can't infer, so the technique states it. The post passes keep the default (a fullscreen sample never leaves the unit square); material techniques that tile a texture across geometry use .
- **Loom.Core.Materials.TechniqueDescriptor**: A backend-neutral description of a drawing/dispatch technique, registered with the engine under a logical name via and referenced from a pass closure by that name (ctx.FullScreen("lighting", …)). This is the describe-layer technique vocabulary: it names the shader logically — not by a backend artifact path — and states the technique's shape (how many inputs it samples, whether it reads geometry, its blend equation). The backend resolves to its own bytecode (SPIR-V for Vulkan, DXIL for DX12) and bakes the pipeline, so no graphics-API artifact name ever appears in app code. The descriptor-binding counts (how many sampled inputs, storage images, and storage buffers the shader binds) are not stated here — the backend derives them from the shader's reflection metadata, so the app no longer hand-counts them. What remains are the pieces reflection can't infer: the logical shader/entry names and the fixed-function pipeline intent (does it read geometry, how does it blend, which sampler filter).
- **Loom.Core.Materials.Texture**: An opaque handle to a GPU-resident texture (image + mip chain), minted by the engine when the app uploads and handed back through a to passes that draw with it. Like , it is just an identity the backend resolves to a real image/view — the describe layer never sees the GPU resource. Textures are app-owned, stable resources (built once at load, kept for the engine's lifetime), so referencing one from a pass's record closure doesn't break the closure's purity the way capturing per-frame data would.
- **Loom.Core.Materials.TextureData**: A neutral, GPU-API-free description of a texture and its mip chain — the engine-boundary type consumes. Produced by an asset loader (Loom.Assets) or built directly from raw pixels via ; the backend's texture store turns it into a sampled image. Mips are generated here on the CPU (a deterministic integer box filter) so both backends upload byte-identical level data — the cleanest path to cross-backend pixel parity and the reason no GPU blit/mip-gen plumbing is needed.
- **Loom.Core.Materials.TextureFormat**: The pixel encoding of a loaded / sampled source image — what a 's texels mean, which the backend maps to a sampled image format (Vulkan/DXGI R8G8B8A8_*). Backend-neutral. Deliberately distinct from : this is the source-texture / sampled-encoding vocabulary (it will grow toward block-compressed formats — BC/ASTC/ETC2), whereas is the render-graph attachment / target vocabulary (HDR, packed, depth). They overlap on the plain RGBA8 encodings on purpose and diverge as each domain's needs grow, so keep them separate rather than unifying.
- **Loom.Core.Primitives.Half4**: A four-component 16-bit-float colour (RGBA16F), the neutral storage for an 's premultiplied colour. Half precision is what lets a composited overlay carry values above paper white (HDR) and a wide gamut without banding, while staying half the size of full floats in the vertex stream. Backend-neutral (System.Half, no graphics-API types); the backend uploads these eight bytes straight into its vertex buffer, the way ImGui uploads packed RGBA8.
- **Loom.Core.Primitives.Rect**: An axis-aligned rectangle in pixels — neutral geometry (no graphics-API types), used for a draw command's scissor () and reused by the SUIsei layout/hit-test code. Stored as origin + size so a zero-size rect is unambiguous; / are derived. Lives in Loom.Core beside as managed value data.
- **Loom.Core.Scene.InstancedGroup**: A group of instances of one mesh drawn with one technique — the unit a ctx.DrawInstanced consumes. Holds each instance's world transform + cached world bounds, and offers a frustum cull that compacts the visible transforms into a caller-provided span (no per-frame allocation).
- **Loom.Core.Scene.Scene**: An optional, app-owned draw-list container — the engine offers a Scene and a frustum-cull helper, but never mandates a scene graph or seizes draw submission. A scene is a flat set of s; the app builds it once, culls it each frame against a view's extracted , and feeds the surviving transforms to ctx.DrawInstanced. Nothing in the engine requires its use — a demo that draws meshes directly still works.
- **Loom.Core.Scene.SceneInstance**: One placed instance of a mesh: a world transform and the world-space that transform produced (cached at add time so the per-frame cull does no matrix work beyond the plane tests).
- **Loom.Graph.AccessKindExtensions**: Interprets each as a read and/or a write for dependency derivation. This is Execute-layer semantics, deliberately kept out of Loom.Core (which only declares intent). The load-bearing case is / : both read and write, so an accumulation pass depends on the prior writer (RAW) and blocks later writers (WAR) at once.
- **Loom.Graph.AliasBucket**: A set of transients that may share one physical allocation: no two are ever live at once.
- **Loom.Graph.AliasPlan**: The transient-aliasing plan derived from a : a partition of the aliasable transients into s such that the resources in any one bucket have pairwise non-overlapping lifetimes, so they can be backed by the same physical memory (e.g. the G-buffer's memory is reused by the bloom mips once the G-buffer is consumed). The number of buckets equals the peak number of simultaneously-live transients — the minimum any aliasing scheme can achieve. Backend-neutral: this decides only which resources share memory (from lifetimes alone). The backend turns each bucket into one allocation, binds the members to it, and emits the aliasing barrier at each hand-off — and may split a bucket if the members' real memory requirements are incompatible (a rarity for same-heap render targets). Non-aliasable resources (, the backbuffer) are excluded; the backend allocates those normally.
- **Loom.Graph.AttachmentAction**: The load/store decision for one render target of a raster pass — what the backend feeds into the pass's VkRenderingAttachmentInfo under dynamic rendering. Colour targets carry ; depth targets carry or .
- **Loom.Graph.BarrierPlan**: The second half of the Execute layer: from a , derive the image-layout transitions and attachment load/store actions for every pass — the barriers the user never writes Backend-neutral, so the same plan drives both the Vulkan and DirectX12 backends. It walks each resource's timeline in execution order. A transition is emitted before a pass whenever the required state differs from the resource's current state (a layout change) or the pass writes the resource (a write always hazards with the prior usage, even at the same layout). Pure read-after-read needs nothing. The present target gets a terminal transition to .
- **Loom.Graph.DebugLabelScopes**: Derives nested GPU debug-label scopes from dotted pass names — e.g. bloom.down1 opens a bloom group containing a down1 leaf. Pure and backend-neutral: RenderDoc/PIX build their event tree from begin/end nesting depth, not from the label text, so a flat label per pass reads as siblings-with-dots. To get a real tree the engine opens a group scope whenever the dotted prefix deepens and closes it when it ends. Split rule: the last '.'-separated segment is the pass's own (leaf) label; everything before it is the group path. No-dot names (gbuffer, view) stay top-level with no group wrapper.
- **Loom.Graph.DebugLabelScopes.PassLabels**: The label work for one pass, in emit order: close open groups, open each of , then open the pass's own scope (which the backend closes after recording the pass).
- **Loom.Graph.DebugLabelScopes.Plan**: The full derived sequence: per-pass label work (aligned with the input order) and the count of groups still open after the last pass (to close before the frame ends).
- **Loom.Graph.EngineBase**: The backend-neutral half of a live engine: technique definition, shader hot-reload, GPU-timing decode, and frame capture. A backend derives from this, fills in the GPU hooks (, , , …), and inherits this lifecycle identically — so the shared sequencing lives once and a new backend can't drift from it. Graph derivation and the per-frame record loop stay the backend's own (the remaining abstract members); this owns the state and ordering that is the same everywhere.
- **Loom.Graph.GraphSchedule**: The execution plan derived from a 's read/write edges: the passes in a valid execution order, each annotated with the prerequisites it depends on. This is the first half of the Execute layer — pure scheduling, no GPU types — so it stays in Loom.Graph and is fully unit-testable. Barrier and layout-transition derivation builds on the same per-resource timeline. Dependencies are derived from same-resource access conflicts: read-after-write, write-after-read, and write-after-write. Pure read-after-read needs no edge. Every edge points forward in program order, so the dependency graph is a DAG and program order is always a valid topological order — the derivation's product is the precise dependency/validation structure, not a reshuffle — the structure a future multi-queue scheduler, the transient aliaser, and culling all build on.
- **Loom.Graph.GraphSchedule.ResourceState**: Per-resource scheduling state as the timeline is walked in program order.
- **Loom.Graph.GraphValidationException**: Thrown when a cannot be scheduled into correct GPU work — e.g. a transient resource is read before any pass writes it (it would sample garbage). Fail loud and early, at derive time, rather than producing a graph that corrupts or stalls at runtime.
- **Loom.Graph.LifetimePlan**: Per-transient lifetime analysis derived from a : for each resource, the execution-order span over which it is live (first touch to last touch). This is the input the backend's transient aliaser needs to recycle memory across non-overlapping lifetimes — the classic "the G-buffer's memory is reused by the bloom mips once the G-buffer is consumed" case. Backend-neutral by design: it yields abstract spans and an overlap/alias query, but makes no placement decision (offsets, pools, real memory requirements) — that is the backend's job, because aliasing two images also needs an aliasing memory barrier at the hand-off, which only the backend emits. A resource declared but never used by any pass gets no entry (nothing to allocate).
- **Loom.Graph.LoadAction**: What happens to an attachment's existing contents when a pass begins rendering to it. With dynamic rendering this is the VkRenderingAttachmentInfo.loadOp; derivation picks it from the access and the resource's history (first write = clear, write-over-existing or blend = load).
- **Loom.Graph.MaterialStore**: Owns the texture-id list behind each handle. A material is just an ordered bundle of textures; the store records that order at and the draw path resolves a material id to its texture ids, then to each backend's bound texture views. Pure bookkeeping over neutral handles, so it is shared rather than reimplemented per backend; kept separate from the GPU resources so the draw path binds with zero per-draw allocation.
- **Loom.Graph.PassBarriers**: The derived synchronisation work for a single pass: the layout/hazard transitions to emit before recording it, and the load/store actions for its render targets. Backend-neutral — the Vulkan backend turns into vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 and into the dynamic-rendering attachment infos. It also carries the derived GPU debug-label nesting (): before recording, the backend closes open groups, opens each of , then opens the pass's own scope (closed after the pass). Diagnostic-only.
- **Loom.Graph.PngWriter**: Minimal, dependency-free PNG encoder (8-bit RGBA) for debug framebuffer captures. Uses the built-in for the IDAT zlib stream and a hand-rolled CRC-32 — no image library needed. Not optimized (filter type 0 on every scanline); fine for validation grabs. Pure CPU work over a byte span, so it is shared by every backend rather than copied into each.
- **Loom.Graph.ResourceLifetime**: The execution-order span over which a resource is live: from the first pass that touches it to the last, measured in units. Two transients whose spans do not overlap can share the same physical memory — the basis of transient aliasing. The span is inclusive at both ends; a resource live at order k occupies that whole pass, so two resources that share any order overlap and must not alias.
- **Loom.Graph.ResourceState**: The logical state a resource is in at a point in the frame — the backend-neutral stand-in for an image layout plus its associated pipeline-stage/access scope. Barrier derivation reasons purely in these states; the backend maps each to a concrete (VkImageLayout, VkPipelineStageFlags2, VkAccessFlags2) triple. Keeping the mapping in the backend is what lets the Vulkan and DirectX12 backends reinterpret the same transitions independently — the backend-isolation invariant.
- **Loom.Graph.ResourceTransition**: A derived state change for one resource, to be realised as a vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 image memory barrier before the consuming pass. The backend turns into the barrier's old layout + source stage/access scope and into the new layout + destination scope. may equal — a same-layout barrier still orders a write-after-write or read-after-write hazard (memory/execution dependency, no layout change).
- **Loom.Graph.ScheduledPass**: A pass placed in execution order, carrying the prerequisite passes derived from its read/write edges. holds immediate prerequisites (the last writer for a read; the last writer plus all readers-since for a write) — exactly what barrier derivation turns into vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 waits. Transitive ordering is handled by the schedule's sort.
- **Loom.Graph.ShaderReflection**: The descriptor-bound resource shape of a shader, read from the slangc -reflection-json sidecar that the shader build emits next to each compiled module. It counts how many sampled inputs, storage images, storage buffers, read-only input buffers, and uniform (constant) buffers the shader binds — so the app states only pipeline intent (geometry/blend/filter/compute) and the backend derives the descriptor/root-signature layout from reflection rather than the author hand-counting them. The JSON is the same across backends, so this parse is shared; each backend maps the neutral counts onto its own layout objects.
- **Loom.Graph.ShaderReloadRegistry**: Tracks which techniques each shader backs, for hot-reload. A backend records every technique it defines here; when a watched shader artifact changes, the backend maps it to a logical shader name and queues it, and draining (on the render thread) replays each affected technique's descriptor through a backend-supplied redefine callback, bracketed by a GPU drain and a pipeline-cache reset. Pure bookkeeping over neutral descriptors — the file watching, the artifact-name parsing, and the GPU/cache work stay in the backend, behind the callbacks.
- **Loom.Graph.StoreAction**: What happens to an attachment's contents when a pass finishes (the VkRenderingAttachmentInfo.storeOp).
- **Loom.Graph.TimingDecode**: Decodes GPU timestamp readbacks into per-pass timings. Collecting the raw timestamps is backend-specific (a query pool vs a query heap, with different valid-bit masking), but turning begin/end tick pairs into milliseconds and aligning them to the schedule's leaf passes is identical across backends, so it lives here.
- **SUIsei.AnimationClock**: Advances active storyboards by the per-frame delta. Held by the and stepped once per from its deltaSeconds, so output is fully deterministic: tests tick synthetic deltas and assert the resolved value over time — no frame loop, no GPU. Each active storyboard tracks its own elapsed time; every tick it normalizes each child animation's progress (honouring /// ) and pushes the eased, interpolated value to the target. When an animation finishes, releases the target while leaves the final value in place. A storyboard is dropped once all its children have finished.
- **SUIsei.AnimationTimeline**: A that drives one target property. The only needs to push the current value and to release the target on stop, so the non-generic base exposes just those two seams; the typed value + apply/release closures live on . The closures are resolved (by the generator, or by hand) to a typed write — no reflection.
- **SUIsei.AnimationTimeline`1**: The typed animation: produces a at a given progress () and writes it through . reverts the target. Concrete subclasses (Double/Color/Point) implement and apply their own easing inside it.
- **SUIsei.BackEase**: Back easing: overshoots slightly before settling. f(t) = t³ − t·A·sin(πt), where A scales the overshoot.
- **SUIsei.ColorAnimation**: Animates an from to over the duration. Interpolation is component-wise in the authored colour space (a cheap, deterministic lerp; perceptual interpolation is a later refinement).
- **SUIsei.CubicEase**: Cubic easing: f(t) = t³.
- **SUIsei.DoubleAnimation**: Animates a scalar from to (or by ) over the duration. A null starts at zero; a null with a ends at From + By.
- **SUIsei.DoubleAnimationUsingKeyFrames**: Animates a scalar through a sequence of s. Each key's is normalized against the ; the value before the first key holds at its value, the value after the last key holds at its value, and each segment is lerped with the upper key's own easing. Keyframes are assumed to be in ascending order.
- **SUIsei.DoubleKeyFrame**: One key of a: the scalar the animation reaches at (measured from the start of the animation), with an optional shaping the segment that ends at this key.
- **SUIsei.EasingFunctionBase**: The base of the built-in easing functions. A subclass defines the raw ease-in shape in ; this base mirrors it for and splices the two halves for , matching WinUI.
- **SUIsei.EasingMode**: Which end of an easing function is shaped.
- **SUIsei.FillBehavior**: What an animation does to its target when it finishes.
- **SUIsei.IEasingFunction**: Maps linear progress t in [0,1] to an eased progress.
- **SUIsei.PointAnimation**: Animates a from to over the duration.
- **SUIsei.QuadraticEase**: Quadratic easing: f(t) = t².
- **SUIsei.RepeatBehavior**: How many times a repeats: a finite iteration or . The default (default(RepeatBehavior)) is a single iteration.
- **SUIsei.Storyboard**: A group of timelines begun and stopped as a unit — the thing runs and swaps per state. Children are the per-property s; the clock advances each by the storyboard's elapsed time.
- **SUIsei.Timeline**: The base of everything an advances: a span of animated time with a , a offset, repeat/reverse behaviour, and a fill rule for what happens when it ends. Plain authoring data — the clock owns the running state.
- **SUIsei.VisualState**: One named look a control can be in — e.g. Normal, PointerOver, Pressed. Entering the state runs its (a null storyboard is the resting/default look).
- **SUIsei.VisualStateGroup**: A set of mutually exclusive s — e.g. the CommonStates group (Normal/PointerOver/Pressed). Exactly one state in a group is current at a time; entering a new one stops the previous state's storyboard. Groups are independent of one another.
- **SUIsei.VisualStateManager**: Drives a control between named visual states. The attached property carries the groups on a control's template root; stops the current state's storyboard and starts the target's. When the control is attached to a host its animates the transition; when detached (or useTransitions is false) the target state's end values are applied synchronously so headless tests still observe the result.
- **SUIsei.ContainerVisual**: A grouping node with no content of its own.
- **SUIsei.ContentPropertyAttribute**: Declares which property of a control receives child elements authored without an explicit property-element wrapper in XAML — the WinUI [ContentProperty(Name = "…")]. Read by SUIsei.SourceGen: a single child is assigned to a scalar content property, multiple children are appended to a collection one. Inherited by derived controls unless re-declared.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Border**: A single-child decorator with a background, a border, padding, and rounded corners: measure deflates by border + padding around the child; arrange insets the child by the same; the visual draws a (rounded) fill + border. Phase B treats as uniform for the drawn stroke.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Button**: A clickable with a default look: a rounded hosting a ({TemplateBinding Content}) with a CommonStates group that animates the background on hover/press. Click synthesis, , and all come from the base.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ButtonBase**: The clickable-control base: the bubbling routed event synthesized from a pointer press+release over the control (or Enter/Space when focused), the common pointer visual states (Normal/PointerOver/Pressed), and WinUI / support. A concrete button supplies its look via a ; is the single override point (e.g. a toggle).
- **SUIsei.Controls.Canvas**: Absolute positioning by the attached /: children measure unconstrained and arrange at their (Left, Top) with their desired size; the Canvas itself desires nothing.
- **SUIsei.Controls.CheckBox**: A with a check-box look: a square box hosting an inner fill glyph, beside a label. The glyph is hidden when unchecked, the accent fill when checked, and a dimmer fill when indeterminate, and the box border picks up the accent while (in)determinate. The box itself reacts to the pointer through a CommonStates group (hover lightens it, press darkens it). (A drawn check mark awaits a glyph in the font atlas; the filled box is the current representation.)
- **SUIsei.Controls.ContentControl**: Hosts a single. Without a it hosts the content directly (a as-is; a string wrapped in a ) and draws an optional solid . With a template, the control's visual tree comes from the template and a {TemplateBinding Content} routes into the template's ; lets that binding stay live.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ContentHelper**: Shared content-hosting policy: a is hosted as-is; a string (or any other object) is wrapped in a . Used by both and so the rule lives in one place. (Data templates replace this in MU4.)
- **SUIsei.Controls.ContentPresenter**: Presents a single — the lightweight presenter a control template points at. When a is set, the content is realized through that ; otherwise a is hosted as-is and any other value is wrapped in a (the shared policy). An optional solid lets it stand in for a panel.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Control**: The base of templatable controls. Sets to true by default so all controls participate in Tab navigation. A defines the visual tree: it is applied lazily on first measure, becomes the control's single visual child, and carries the groups.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ControlTemplate**: Defines a control's visual tree. The — generated from a <ControlTemplate>, or hand-written — news the subtree given the templated control, wiring its {TemplateBinding}s and groups at instantiation.
- **SUIsei.Controls.DataTemplate**: Defines the visual tree for a data item — used by and items controls to realize one subtree per item. The news the subtree given the item and wires its template-scoped {x:Bind}s against the item.
- **SUIsei.Controls.FrameworkTemplate**: The base of the compile-time templates. A template is a generated factory that news a subtree — never reflection — so and differ only in what the factory is handed (the templated control vs the data item).
- **SUIsei.Controls.Grid**: A row/column grid: Pixel tracks are fixed, Auto tracks size to their largest child, and Star tracks share the leftover space by weight after Pixel/Auto are subtracted. Children select a cell with the attached / and may span tracks with /. An empty definition list defaults to one Star track. MU2 limitation: a spanning child does not drive Auto-track sizing (only single-cell children do).
- **SUIsei.Controls.IItemContainerSource**: The contract a virtualizing panel pulls item containers from — implemented by . The panel realizes only the containers in its viewport and recycles the rest, so a large list never materializes all its containers at once.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Image**: Draws an, scaled into its layout bounds per . Measures to the source's natural pixel size (in DIPs) so an unconstrained image takes its intrinsic size; an explicit Width/Height on the element overrides that as usual.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ItemsControl**: Lays out one container per item of in an. Each container is realized through (a ) or, with no template, by wrapping the item. When the source implements the realized containers are updated incrementally (add/remove/replace/move/reset) rather than rebuilt.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ItemsPanelTemplate**: Builds the an lays its item containers out in. The default is a vertical ; a virtualizing list supplies a instead.
- **SUIsei.Controls.IVirtualizingItemsHost**: A panel that virtualizes its children by pulling them from an. An detects this on its panel and hands it the source instead of pushing all the containers itself.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ListView**: An that wraps each item in a selectable. Clicking an item selects it (driving the item's SelectionStates visual); MU4 implements single selection (full multi-select is a later refinement).
- **SUIsei.Controls.ListViewItem**: The container a wraps each item in. A SelectionStates group animates a selection highlight behind the content; the owning list calls when the selection changes.
- **SUIsei.Controls.MenuFlyout**: A context menu: opens a list of in the root's overlay layer just below the target, with a full-surface light-dismiss layer behind it. Invoking an item (which fires its / ) or pressing outside closes it.
- **SUIsei.Controls.MenuFlyoutItem**: A single command row in a: a with a label and a flat full-width template that highlights on hover. Click invocation and come from the base; the flyout closes itself on invoke.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Panel**: The base of multi-child layout containers: owns the collection and an optional solid . Subclasses implement the measure/arrange policy.
- **SUIsei.Controls.Popup**: A transient overlay: when is set, its is composited above the root's content at (, ) and hit-tested on top. The popup element itself occupies no layout space. With a full-surface layer behind the child closes the popup on an outside press. The popup must be attached to a live root (in the element tree) for to take effect; drives the overlay imperatively.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ScrollViewer**: A clipping viewport over a single oversized. Measures the content unbounded in the scroll axis to learn its extent, arranges it offset by the scroll position, and clips to the viewport. Scrolls by mouse wheel, by keyboard (Page/Home/End/arrows when a descendant is focused), and programmatically; the offset is always clamped to /. Pairs with , which reports its full extent for exactly this viewport.
- **SUIsei.Controls.SelectionMode**: How many items a allows selected at once.
- **SUIsei.Controls.StackPanel**: Stacks children end-to-end along: the stacking axis is measured unconstrained (∞), desired = sum along it and max across it; arrange lays children out one after another, each stretched on the cross axis.
- **SUIsei.Controls.TextBlock**: A run of text. MU1 measures + emits glyphs against the engine's default MTSDF font (): an advance-based width (no HarfBuzz shaping — that is MU5) and a the compositor lays out into draws.
- **SUIsei.Controls.TextBox**: A single-line editable text field. Consumes the host's and events (the input pipeline already routes them to the focused element) to drive a caret + selection over : insert/overtype, Backspace/Delete, arrow/Home/End motion (Shift extends the selection), Select-All, and cut/copy/paste through a process-wide clipboard (an OS clipboard is a later host seam). is a dependency property with a event, so it participates in TwoWay {x:Bind}. IME is deferred — committed characters only.
- **SUIsei.Controls.ToggleButton**: A that holds a checked state — the base for . A click cycles (two-state, or three-state through null when is set), raising // and driving the CheckStates visual-state group. Subclasses reflect the state in template parts via .
- **SUIsei.Controls.UIElementCollection**: The ordered child collection of a ; adds re-parent the child and invalidate the owner's measure.
- **SUIsei.Controls.VirtualizingStackPanel**: A vertical items panel that realizes only the containers intersecting its viewport. MU4 assumes a uniform , so the visible window is pure arithmetic from ; containers that scroll out are recycled back to the . It reports the full extent (ItemCount × RowHeight) so an outer scroller sees the true size. Variable-height virtualization, a scroll chrome, and wheel/scrollbar input are later refinements; the offset is set directly here.
- **SUIsei.DependencyObject**: The base of everything that carries dependency properties. Holds a sparse, int-keyed effective-value store and resolves the WinUI value-precedence ladder: Animation > Local > Style > Inherited > Default A set recomputes the top of the ladder, coerces it, fires the typed change callback only when the coerced resolved value changes, and ORs the property's into the element (via ). Reflection-free: dispatch goes through the typed delegates on . The animation rung exists from day one (a hard prerequisite for storyboards, MU4) even though nothing drives it until then.
- **SUIsei.DependencyProperty**: A reflection-free dependency property — the WinUI semantics (typed metadata, change/coerce callbacks, value precedence) with the -keyed, string-dispatched mechanism replaced by a dense integer slot () and typed delegates. Abstract base; the concrete property is always a . Identity is by reference.
- **SUIsei.DependencyProperty`2**: The concrete, typed dependency property.
- **SUIsei.DependencyPropertyKind**: Whether a property is declared on its owner () or attached to arbitrary targets (, e.g. Grid.Row). Both share the one dense index space.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.AtlasImage**: Decoded RGBA8 pixels from a font atlas — the neutral image data FontAtlas exposes for the engine glue to upload as a GPU texture. SUIsei decodes the atlas PNG itself (no engine dependency); the engine side creates whatever texture type it needs from these bytes.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.DrawCommand**: One batched draw call in a draw list: a contiguous slice of the index stream drawn under a scissor rectangle with one texture bound. Blittable and sequentially laid out — the engine glue can reinterpret its memory as the equivalent engine draw command without copying.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.DrawListData**: One frame's flattened draw list — a variable-size vertex stream, its 16-bit index stream, and the batched draw commands that scissor + texture + index-range it. Backend-neutral (no graphics-API types), so the whole producer pipeline up to GPU upload is CPU-testable against . Rebuilt only when its source changes; an unchanged frame re-submits the same Revision.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.DrawListId**: Identifies one draw list a surface's compositor produces each frame.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.ImageSource**: A decoded RGBA8 image an draws. SUIsei stays GPU-free: the source holds neutral pixels (decoded with StbImageSharp, the same decoder as ) and a stable ; the engine glue uploads it once and binds it by that index, the same texture channel the white texel (0) and glyph atlas (1) ride. Indices start at 2 so they never collide with those two.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.OverlayVertex**: The vertex of a 2D overlay draw list — a pixel-space position, texture coordinate, premultiplied colour, and a float4 of per-vertex data the consuming technique defines. Blittable and sequentially laid out so it can be uploaded directly to a GPU vertex buffer.
- **SUIsei.Drawing.PremultipliedHdrColor**: A premultiplied RGBA16F colour — the wire format for the overlay vertex stream. Four Half components (8 bytes), blittable and sequentially laid out so the engine can upload it directly as GPU vertex data. Named PremultipliedHdrColor (not a bare four-Half vector) so the premultiplied-alpha contract is explicit in the type system; produced by .
- **SUIsei.DrawListCompositor**: Loom's default : walks a surface's composition tree, folds transform/clip/opacity into a pre-transformed vertex/command stream, and exposes it as a neutral . Emits the rectangle family (fills + borders) and MSDF glyph runs. Output is asserted on CPU via — the primary test seam, no backend needed.
- **SUIsei.FocusManager**: Per-host focus state machine. Tracks the focused element, raises the four focus routed events (GettingFocus/LosingFocus tunnel, GotFocus/LostFocus bubble), and drives Tab/Shift-Tab navigation across a set of s respecting , , , and focus scopes.
- **SUIsei.FocusState**: How focus was most recently acquired on an element (WinUI-compatible).
- **SUIsei.FontAtlas**: A baked MTSDF font atlas: the decoded atlas page plus per-glyph layout, loaded from the pair an MSDF generator emits — a PNG page (RGBA8 MTSDF) and a JSON layout. The page is decoded linear/UNORM, no mips: MTSDF texels are signed distances, never sRGB colour. Plane bounds are EM units in a y-down, baseline-at-origin frame.
- **SUIsei.FrameworkElement**: Adds the WinUI framework-level layout inputs on top of: explicit / (NaN = Auto), / (and the height pair), , and alignment. It implements the WinUI MeasureCore/ArrangeCore wrapper — deflate by margin, clamp to min/max/explicit, call the element's MeasureOverride/ArrangeOverride, reinflate — so every control only writes its intrinsic sizing. Backing storage uses the C# 14 field keyword (no hand-declared fields).
- **SUIsei.Glyph**: One baked glyph from a. Plane bounds are EM units in a y-down, baseline-at-origin frame (the on-screen quad, scaled by the font px size); the UV rect addresses the glyph's MTSDF cell in the atlas page (0..1, v=0 at the top — the atlas is baked with yOrigin: top). Whitespace glyphs set false and carry only an .
- **SUIsei.GlyphRunContent**: A run of laid-out text drawn from a. The compositor lays the glyphs out against its font (advance-based LTR, no shaping — that is MU5), emitting commands. is the on-screen size in surface pixels (DIPs × scale); the colour is the authored (linearized + premultiplied by the compositor like every other brush).
- **SUIsei.GridLength**: A Grid row/column track length — fixed pixels, Auto (max child desired), or a * weight of the leftover space (WinUI GridLength). Default is 1*, matching WinUI.
- **SUIsei.GridUnitType**: How a is interpreted: a fixed DIP size, content-sized, or a proportional star.
- **SUIsei.HdrColor**: An authoring colour — float RGBA where 0..1 is SDR / paper-white range and a component >1 is above paper white (opt-in HDR). Named HdrColor (not Color) for explicitness and to dodge the clash. Folded to a by the compositor; the paper-white reference scale is applied in the shader.
- **SUIsei.HorizontalAlignment**: WinUI alignment within a layout slot's horizontal axis. fills the slot.
- **SUIsei.HotReload**: XAML Hot Reload support. A generated view registers itself here in InitializeComponent() (a no-capture call), and each registers itself on construction. When the runtime applies a metadata delta (an edited .xaml re-runs the source generator under dotnet watch), the records the changed types; the next drains them and rebuilds the affected views on the UI thread — never on the hot-reload agent's thread. Bookkeeping is gated on , which defaults to : it is false under NativeAOT / optimized publish, so the whole mechanism is inert and trimmable there, preserving the reflection-free runtime. Tests force it on.
- **SUIsei.HotReloadHandler**: The [MetadataUpdateHandler] target (registered as an assembly attribute in ). The runtime invokes these after applying a metadata delta; they hand the changed types to , which defers the actual view rebuild to the next .
- **SUIsei.ImageContent**: A tinted image drawn into (element-local pixels) from — the primitive the compositor emits as a command.
- **SUIsei.InputManager**: Per-host pointer routing: hit-tests each queued over the host's interactive overlay views, raises tunnel-then-bubble pointer routed events, tracks the "over" chain (so enter/exit fire per element), implicitly captures on press so a press→release pair routes to the same target (the basis for Button.Click), and supports explicit drag capture via /. Persistent host state; headless (no engine/backend, §D8).
- **SUIsei.Input.FocusNavigationDirection**: Direction of programmatic or keyboard-driven focus movement.
- **SUIsei.Input.KeyInput**: One device-neutral keyboard event the host queues into between frames. The host (Sandbox/Silk.NET) translates raw platform key events into this, keeping windowing types out of SUIsei.
- **SUIsei.Input.ModifierKeys**: Modifier keys held at the time of a keyboard or pointer event.
- **SUIsei.Input.VirtualKey**: Virtual key codes (WinUI-compatible subset). Values match Windows virtual-key codes so host adapters can cast directly from platform key enumerations.
- **SUIsei.PointerButtons**: The set of pointer buttons currently held.
- **SUIsei.PointerDeviceType**: The kind of device that produced a — WinUI-shaped and device-neutral so no host (Silk.NET) type leaks into SUIsei. MU2 drives only ; pen and touch arrive with the same struct at MU5.
- **SUIsei.PointerInput**: One device-neutral pointer event the host queues into a between frames. WinUI-shaped so mouse, pen and touch share one struct; the host (Sandbox/Silk.NET) translates raw input into this, keeping graphics/windowing types out of SUIsei. is in surface pixels (the same space as the composited DrawListData / the framebuffer); the host hit-tests and routes it in .
- **SUIsei.PointerUpdateKind**: What changed in a — the WinUI PointerUpdateKind. A plain move carries ; a button edge carries the specific pressed/released kind that the input pipeline turns into PointerPressed/PointerReleased routed events (and, on a matching pair, a synthesized Click).
- **SUIsei.InvalidationFlags**: Which layout/render stages a property change invalidates — ORed up the tree on a resolved-value change. A pure-render change (a brush colour) sets only ; a sizing change sets .
- **SUIsei.IUICompositor**: The portability boundary: renders a surface's tree. Loom ships ; a foreign engine substitutes its own and consumes the tree directly.
- **SUIsei.IValueConverter**: Converts a value between binding source and target types. Implement this for converter= attributes in XAML bindings; pass a singleton instance via {StaticResource key}.
- **SUIsei.LayerEffect**: A composition-tree post effect applied to a group's render-to-texture layer. A visual that carries an effect is always composited as one bitmap (exactly like a sub-1 group opacity), and the effect is applied when the layer is composited back into its parent. selects the effect the backend runs; .. are its parameters. Id 0 is the identity (opacity-only); id 1 is a Gaussian blur whose pixel sigma is .
- **SUIsei.Orientation**: The axis a stacks along.
- **SUIsei.Point**: A point in DIPs (layout-space). Distinct from only for readability at call sites.
- **SUIsei.PropertyMetadata`2**: The typed metadata for a : default value, a typed change callback (old, new — no boxing on the typed path), an optional coerce, and what it invalidates. Callbacks are static by convention (captured once at registration — no per-instance delegate, no reflection; PlanningUI.md §D1.1).
- **SUIsei.Rect**: An axis-aligned rectangle in pixels — neutral geometry used for layout, hit-testing, clip rects, and draw commands. Stored as origin + size so a zero-size rect is unambiguous; Right/Bottom are derived.
- **SUIsei.RectContent**: A solid (optionally rounded) rectangle with an optional border — the Border/Panel background primitive.
- **SUIsei.ResourceDictionary**: A keyed resource store used by and resolved at compile time by the XAML source generator for {StaticResource key} references. Runtime lookup walks in reverse-index order (later entries take priority).
- **SUIsei.RootVisual**: The root of one surface's composition tree.
- **SUIsei.CharacterReceivedRoutedEventArgs**: Event args for .
- **SUIsei.GettingFocusEventArgs**: Event args for and (both tunnel). Handlers may set to prevent the focus transfer from completing.
- **SUIsei.KeyRoutedEventArgs**: Event args for , , and their Preview counterparts.
- **SUIsei.PointerPoint**: A snapshot of a pointer at the moment of a routed pointer event — the WinUI PointerPoint, trimmed to what MU2 needs. is in surface pixels.
- **SUIsei.PointerRoutedEventArgs**: Payload for the pointer routed events: the and the originating . Pooled by the input pipeline. Key modifiers arrive with keyboard input in MU3.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEvent**: A routed-event identity: a dense assigned at registration, a diagnostic , and the strategy. Registered once in a static field initializer (deterministic, AOT-safe — no assembly scanning), the same self-registration shape as . The dense id keys the per-element handler store with no string lookup.
- **SUIsei.RoutedEventArgs**: The base routed-event payload. is the element the event was raised on; is the current element as the route advances; short-circuits the remaining route (a handler that registered handledEventsToo still runs — MU3). Mutable + reusable so the input pipeline can pool one instance per dispatch (honouring the "0 GC in the render loop" rule).
- **SUIsei.RoutedEventHandler**: The single routed-event delegate shape — typed, so invocation is a direct call with no MethodInfo.Invoke and no argument boxing (the NAOT requirement). The generator wires handlers to it (btn.Click += this.OnClick), signature-checked at generate time.
- **SUIsei.RoutingStrategy**: How a travels the element tree. goes root→target (WinUI Preview*), target→root, fires only on the target. MU2 exercises (+ for enter/exit); the tunnel pass is wired but dormant until paired tunnel events arrive in MU3.
- **SUIsei.Setter**: A single property assignment within a. Writes the Style rung of the DP precedence ladder, so Local values and animations still win over a Style-sourced value.
- **SUIsei.Size**: A width/height pair in device-independent pixels (DIPs). Either component may be during measure (an unconstrained axis). Mirrors WinUI's Size.
- **SUIsei.SpriteVisual**: A leaf node that draws (rect/border now; glyph-run/image later).
- **SUIsei.Stretch**: How an scales its source into its layout bounds (WinUI Stretch).
- **SUIsei.Style**: An ordered collection of s applied to a via the Style rung of the DP precedence ladder. forms a chain: base setters apply first so derived setters override them. When replaced, the previous style's setters are cleared before the new style is applied.
- **SUIsei.TabFocusNavigation**: Controls how Tab navigation behaves within a subtree (WinUI-compatible).
- **SUIsei.Thickness**: Per-edge spacing in DIPs — used for Margin, Padding, and border thickness (WinUI Thickness).
- **SUIsei.UIDrawList**: A pooled builder for the neutral draw list — the analog of ImGui's ImDrawList. Bakes the composed transform into vertex positions and merges consecutive primitives that share (kind, textureId, clip) into one indexed draw command (atlas-everything + state-run batching).
- **SUIsei.UIElement**: The base of every visual element: two-pass measure/arrange, layout invalidation, the owned composition , render-affecting DPs, routed events (pointer + keyboard + focus), hit-testing, and focus/capture queries. The WinUI MeasureCore/ArrangeCore seam lets layer Margin/Min/Max/alignment on top of the element's intrinsic sizing.
- **SUIsei.UIHost**: A per-window UI host — not a singleton, so multi-window/multi-surface is first-class. It owns the input routing and the set of roots outside the render graph, holds no engine or backend handle, and exposes the per-frame split: queue neutral events between frames, then once per frame (drain → hit-test → route → lay out) and (composite each view → ). Both run headless (no GPU), so the whole pipeline is unit-tested by queuing events and asserting DrawLists/DumpState.
- **SUIsei.UIPlacement**: Where and how a is placed. MU2 implements — a screen-space layer with a z-order and a DIP→pixel . (a quad with a world transform + optional billboard, plus its 3D ray hit-test) is declared for API shape but lands in MU5.
- **SUIsei.UIPlacementKind**: Where a renders. MU2 ships ; in-world quads (and their 3D ray hit-test) arrive in MU5.
- **SUIsei.UIPrimKind**: The primitive family the UI compositor encodes into a draw command's — it selects the branch the single ui.slang fragment switches on. A flat so it casts to the tag cheaply.
- **SUIsei.UIRoot**: One UI surface: owns the element tree and the composition tree it composites through a pluggable . Holds no engine or backend handle, so + run to completion headless — input crosses in as a size, the product is a neutral (the headless-testable invariant).
- **SUIsei.UISurface**: Well-known s for the UI host. The overlay HUD is list 0; in-world surfaces take higher ids.
- **SUIsei.UIView**: A root handle returned by: the (element + composition trees), its , and whether it is . Keep it to swap the root's content or tear it down. Non-interactive views skip hit-test/focus entirely (MU5 health bars/nameplates).
- **SUIsei.VerticalAlignment**: WinUI alignment within a layout slot's vertical axis. fills the slot.
- **SUIsei.Visibility**: WinUI element visibility. contributes zero to layout and never hit-tests.
- **SUIsei.Visual**: A retained composition node — the tree a pluggable renders. Carries a 2D (animatable independently of layout), group , an optional , and a damage flag for incremental recomposition. Backend-neutral.
- **SUIsei.VisualContent**: What a draws. Phase B ships the rectangle family (fill + border); glyph-run and image content arrive with MSDF text + images (MU1+). A small record hierarchy so the compositor switches on the concrete type with no reflection.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.AnimationClip**: A named skeletal animation — a set of per-joint s plus the clip's total . Sampled at a time in [0, Duration] (the app loops/clamps as it likes) to produce per-joint local transforms, which the animation runtime composes down the skeleton into the bone palette. Backend-neutral, immutable; the natural output of a glTF animation. One clip drives one skeleton.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.AnimationInterpolation**: How an animation track interpolates between keyframes — mirrors glTF's sampler interpolation modes.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.JointChannel**: One joint's animated transform within an — any of its translation, rotation, and scale may be keyed. A null track means that component is not animated by this clip and the joint's bind-pose value () is used instead. Backend-neutral, immutable.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.QuaternionTrack**: A keyframed animation channel — a joint's rotation over time. The are strictly increasing seconds; [i] is the (unit) rotation at Times[i]. Linear interpolation slerps between the surrounding keyframes. Backend-neutral, immutable.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.Skeleton**: A mesh's skeleton: a flat joint array (in glTF skin order) where each joint records its parent index (-1 for a root), its inverse bind matrix, and its bind-pose local transform. The parents form a forest and may appear in any order — the animation runtime resolves world matrices accordingly, so no topological sort is assumed. Backend-neutral (System.Numerics), immutable — the natural output of a glTF skin. The animation runtime composes a clip's sampled local transforms down this hierarchy into joint world matrices, then multiplies each by its entry to get the bone palette the skinning shader applies. A 's joint indices reference this array (and thus the palette slots). is the fallback when a clip leaves a joint (or a joint's translation/rotation/scale) un-keyed.
- **Loom.Core.Animation.SkinnedVertex**: A skinned mesh's bind-pose vertex: the canonical fields plus the two skinning attributes — four bone indices and four blend weights. 80 bytes, sequentially packed, mirroring (POSITION 0, NORMAL 12, TEXCOORD 24, TANGENT 32, JOINTS 48, WEIGHTS 64). Backend-neutral (System.Numerics + plain uints, no graphics-API types). The joint indices reference the mesh's joint array (and thus the bone-palette slot the compute skinning pass multiplies by); the weights sum to 1 (the glTF importer renormalizes). A vertex bound to fewer than four joints sets the unused weights to 0 (their joint index is then irrelevant).
- **Loom.Core.Animation.Vector3Track**: A keyframed animation channel — a joint's translation or scale over time. The are strictly increasing seconds; [i] is the value at Times[i]. The two arrays have equal length (≥ 1). Backend-neutral, immutable.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Bounds**: An axis-aligned bounding box (Min/Max corners). The unit of coarse visibility: a mesh carries a local-space box, an instance transforms it to world space, and the CPU frustum cull tests it against the camera's . Backend-neutral pure math (System.Numerics), like — culling is an app-owned optimization the engine offers, never a scene graph it mandates ("you hand me draw lists").
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Frustum**: A view frustum as six inward-facing s (left, right, bottom, top, near, far) in world space — the debug camera's "what would be visible" volume and the engine's optional CPU frustum-cull primitive. Each plane is oriented so the inside half-space is positive ( ≥ 0). Built from a view-projection matrix via ; composed entirely of types (no bespoke math). Extracted from the neutral view-projection (right-handed, +Y up, z ∈ [0,1] — the host's CreatePerspectiveFieldOfView convention), so culling is backend-independent: the per-backend clip-space Y-flip only affects rasterization NDC, not which world objects are in view.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Matrix4x4FrustumExtensions**: C# 14 extension members on for frustum math — kept on the BCL type per the project convention (use ; add missing operations as extension members, not a bespoke helper class). The receiver is a row-vector view-projection (clip = world · viewProjection).
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Mesh**: An opaque handle to GPU-resident geometry (vertex + index buffers), minted by the engine when the app uploads a mesh and handed back to passes via . Like , it is just an identity the backend resolves to real buffers — the describe layer never sees the GPU resources. Meshes are app-owned, stable resources (the app builds them once and keeps them), so referencing one from a pass's record closure does not break the closure's purity the way capturing per-frame data would ("you hand me draw lists").
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.OverlayVertex**: The vertex of a 2D overlay draw list — the universal shape for screen-space, painter-ordered geometry (UI, immediate-mode overlays, a textured quad): a pixel-space position, a texture coordinate, a premultiplied colour, and a float4 of per-vertex data the consuming technique defines. Backend-neutral (System.Numerics + ), [StructLayout] sequential so it uploads as verbatim.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.Vertex**: Loom's canonical interleaved vertex: position, normal, UV, and a tangent. One fixed layout for now — enough to drive the reference frame's geometry plus normal mapping. Backend-neutral (System.Numerics, no graphics-API types), so the backend owns the vertex-layout description that mirrors these fields. Shaders that don't read the tangent simply ignore the extra attribute.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexAttribute**: One attribute in a : a semantic name plus its element format. The semantic is the neutral link between the data and the shader — Vulkan binds by [[vk::location]] (assigned in order), DirectX12 binds by HLSL semantic name + index (the index derived from how many earlier attributes share the name, so four "ITRANSFORM" rows become ITRANSFORM0..3). Semantic names map 1:1 onto glTF attribute names (POSITION, NORMAL, TEXCOORD, TANGENT, …), which is what makes an importer's output drop straight into a layout (glTF).
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexFormat**: Backend-neutral vertex-attribute formats — the element type of one attribute in a . Deliberately separate from (which is render-target / texture oriented and has no three-component float concept): a vertex attribute is just a small tuple of 32-bit floats today. The backend maps each to its concrete API format (e.g. → VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32_SFLOAT / DXGI_FORMAT_R32G32B32_FLOAT). Grow this deliberately as layouts need more (packed colours, integer bone indices for skinning).
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexFormatExtensions**: Helpers over — kept here so the enum stays a plain value list.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexInputRate**: How the input assembler advances through a 's buffer.
- **Loom.Core.Geometry.VertexLayout**: A backend-neutral description of one vertex stream: an ordered attribute set, the byte offset of each attribute (tight-packed in declaration order), the resulting stride, and whether the input assembler advances or (and which binding slot it occupies). A is uploaded against a layout, a technique declares the layout(s) it consumes, and the backend builds its pipeline vertex-input + bind stride from them. The layout is the shared contract between a mesh and the technique that draws it — a stride mismatch is a clear engine error, not a silent corruption. Backend-neutral by construction (no graphics-API type), so the same layout drives Vulkan and DirectX12. It is the natural output of an asset importer too — a glTF loader reads accessors and emits a layout + packed buffer — assets are loader-owned, Core never gains a decode dependency.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.AccessKind**: How a single pass touches a single resource. These edges are the entire input to the Execute layer: ordering, barriers, layout transitions and aliasing are all derived from them The vs distinction is load-bearing — it tells the barrier-deriver whether the contents are produced (clearable) or accumulated onto.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.BlendMode**: How a technique's colour output combines with what is already in the target — technique state, not pass state ("additive-ness is technique state, not pass state"). It pairs with a pass that .Blends its target: the graph derives that the existing contents must be preserved and read-modify-written; this enum picks the blend equation the backend bakes into the pipeline. Backend-neutral — the backend maps each value to its own blend-state representation (Vulkan blend factors, D3D12 blend desc).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.BufferHandle**: A GPU storage buffer (not an image). A compute pass .ReadWrites it and a draw .ReadsVertex it (GPU particles). Sized in bytes, not resolution-bound.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ColorHandle**: A colour image target. Produced by .Writes/.Blends, read by .Samples, and (as a storage image — e.g. the persistent exposure value) by .ReadWrites. Also the static type of the and image handles, which are colour-like (their distinct lifetime is carried by ).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.ConstantsHandle**: An app-writable parameter buffer (a uniform/constant buffer). Created with , filled per frame (or on change) by handle via IEngine.Write, and bound to a technique's reflected uniform slot by a pass that .Reads it. Sized to sizeof(T); the struct written through Write must match the shader's uniform-block layout on both backends (std140 / cbuffer packing — prefer float4 rows).
- **Loom.Core.Graph.CullMode**: Which triangle faces a technique discards before rasterizing — fixed-function rasterizer state the backend bakes into the pipeline, not pass state. Like it is intent that reflection can't infer, so the technique states it; the backend maps each value to its own representation (Vulkan VkCullModeFlags, D3D12 D3D12_CULL_MODE). Loom's front-face winding is counter-clockwise in screen space (the glTF convention and Vulkan's default), and both backends are configured to agree on it — so discards the same triangles whichever backend renders, preserving cross-backend parity.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.DepthHandle**: A depth/stencil target. Written by .WritesDepth, tested by .ReadsDepth, and sampleable.
- **Loom.Core.Graph.Domain**: A resolution domain: everything declared in it renders at ×.
